Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9015 (development prerelease)

  • Native compact-vector initialization is retained when Rcpp attributes are regenerated. CI checks generated registration on all three platforms and with the distribution’s Rcpp package.
  • The compact-vector data-pointer callback supports R 4.6’s public API while retaining compatibility with earlier R headers.
  • Release metadata checks and software citations identify the current development prerelease. Historical release identities remain unchanged.
  • The panel cleanup diagnostic test compares normalized paths on Windows.
  • README relates current manuscript algorithm numbers to legacy software identifiers. Numerical algorithms and result schemas are unchanged.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9014 (local development candidate)

  • Default split alignment keeps projected-split ledger text in a compact deferred character representation. Full taxon names are rendered when requested, while branch identities, matrices and provenance remain intact. Version-3 RDS serialization preserves the compact representation and needs SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9014 or later to read it. Explicit version-2 RDS is an ordinary-character fallback for older readers, at greater memory/file cost. Restored Unicode split labels retain their character meaning when the reader’s native locale differs from the writer’s.
  • Selected fusion-source queries render only the requested split records. Requesting or modifying an entire text column can still materialize it.
  • Fixed-topology graph assembly writes fusion-ledger columns directly and avoids unused source tables for original-branch cells. It retains the same observation, state, numerical and source-table schema.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9013 (local development candidate)

  • Gene-specific S4 errors identify the gene without losing condition metadata. Unrepresented ancestral stems are described relative to the declared unrooted observation view; original input Newick remains retained.
  • Direct fusion views exclude multi-component numerical construction before overflow or missing-length checks, consistently with S4.
  • Disk readers accept empty fusion selections. Export diagnostics distinguish occupied paths, including dangling symlinks, while preserving no-clobber publication. Failed cleanup is reported without replacing the primary error.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9012 (local development candidate)

  • Empty disk-panel fusion catalogs now explicitly retain character coordinate IDs on R versions whose default is stringsAsFactors = TRUE. The reader continues to validate the same schema; no fusion or matrix semantics change.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9011 (local development candidate)

  • Native Linux validation found that R 3.6 lacks unlink(expand = FALSE). Disk-output cleanup now uses literal filesystem paths across supported R versions, preserving neighboring paths that contain wildcard characters.
  • Package checks now inspect every raw test event, including errors followed by warnings, so a test reporter summary cannot conceal a failed check.
  • The S4 reference, observation, numerical and mismatch contracts are unchanged. This compatibility candidate preserves the 9010 source and its check evidence.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9010 (local development candidate)

  • S4 now separates reference_semantics from gene_semantics. Rooted reference identity preserves the original root exactly as S3 does; gene inputs default to unrooted observations, with reference_rooted available by declaration.
  • The new s4-observation-v1 result separates reference states and components from empirical observations. Joint observations caused by forgetting a root are recorded once, without inventing separate root-child lengths or deletion fusions. Unrepresented stems remain in reference truth and receive no length.
  • Observation provenance distinguishes one input edge from a complete sum of input edges after normalization. Whole/direct fusion views respect complete observation units and retain each target’s contributing sources.
  • A fixed-topology mismatch skips that gene and records its ID and reason. Reference rows cover all inputs; numeric rows cover successful genes only. Counts and typed empty outputs remain available when every gene is skipped. Other input errors still fail explicitly; there is no S2 fallback.
  • The old tree_semantics = "unrooted" spelling is a deprecated alias. The old rooted spelling raises a migration error because its MRCA-stem convention differs from the new reference definition. New results have no ambiguous state_matrix or component_ledger aliases. Historical results are preserved.
  • S4 gene inputs may explicitly represent unary stem structure. Original reference inputs retain the 9009 contract: every internal node, including the root, must have at least two children. A unary root created by S3 restriction remains valid; the S2 parser’s input contract is unchanged.
  • S3 reference truth, S2/Fast mapping, Support and deletion-fusion identities keep their existing definitions. This candidate is not a published release.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9009 (local development candidate)

  • reference_truth() exposes the S3 graph algorithm for arbitrary reference trees and retained-taxon sets, with separate original-branch and shared fusion matrices, complete members and expected reference-length provenance.
  • Rooted S3 preserves the original root and its path to the retained-tip MRCA. It never adopts S4’s MRCA promotion rule. Reference truth accepts no empirical gene trees and makes no topology-recovery classification.
  • Both graph paths share the optimized table builder. Existing unrooted Catnip10 behavior and the default S2/Fast mapping entry are unchanged.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9008 (local development candidate)

  • S4 assembles component and fusion ledgers by columns and indexes each primitive’s current component once per gene. Complete provenance and all existing whole/direct, rooted/unrooted output semantics are retained.
  • Document the split-based align_branches() path as the default for both free and fixed inputs. S4 remains an explicit choice and the Catnip10 oracle remains a separate validation entry. No automatic algorithm switching was introduced.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9007 (local development candidate)

  • align_fixed_topology() implements Algorithm S4 independently of the Fast mapper: graph restriction with complete member tracking, followed by exact labeled-tree isomorphism and empirical edge-length assignment.
  • Explicit rooted and unrooted semantics, strict topology-mismatch errors, primitive states, whole/direct fusion views, and source-edge provenance are exposed in a separate splitaligner_fixed_result. Existing S2 APIs retain their current behavior.
  • Rooted restriction promotes the root to the retained taxa’s MRCA. Discarded stem members become NA_struct; root promotion is recorded per gene. This differs from the historical rooted/global Catnip10 oracle’s retained stem, and the old benchmark artifacts remain unchanged.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9006 (development)

  • New panels record the whole-component or direct fusion view. Use read_panel_fusion_cells() to trace each value to the original gene tree. Existing v1 panels retain their original direct-only values.
  • Align large collections in batches with align_panel_to_disk(). Look up fusion patterns across all batches and read selected genes and branches.
  • Fixed and free in-memory alignments return branch Support and an annotated Newick reference tree. Each new disk panel also exports support for the complete gene set using the totals from all batches.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9005 (development prerelease)

  • free_fusion_groups() reports the exact projected split, primitive members and recovered length or NA_fuse_topo once per gene and fusion group.
  • count_free_topology() summarizes five disjoint outcomes per gene in an explicit primitive-member or projected-coordinate unit.
  • The default paired schema 2.0.0 retains NA_fuse on every fused primitive. Select rule = "legacy" to replay schema 1.0.0 final matrices.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9004 (development)

  • The exact-bitset SplitAlignerFast backend supplies branch mapping through C ABI 2. The R adapter reuses display strings and gene-ID keys when building full result matrices and ledgers.
  • The package includes fixed-mode exchange and label tools introduced in 0.1.0.9002.
  • Restored the Catnip10 regression suite and quick-start vignette and added backend identity, byte-key and result restoration tests.
  • Included the MIT notice for the four vendored Fast source files.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9000

  • Published the immutable, Pro-RECERT-certified v0.1.0 release.
  • Started post-release development; this development line is not covered by the v0.1.0 RECERT decision.
  • Deferred subsequent user-usability APIs to separately scoped development tasks.

SplitAlignerR 0.1.0

  • Added the conditional FIX007 Windows R-hosted numeric-path isolation: CRLF- safe evidence parsing with raw-byte preservation, explicit snapshot commit metadata, an independent source-clean gate, and fresh-process bare-R DLL and package-Rcpp microprobes. Windows run 30346950266 objectively triggered authorized case A: hosted automatic/static regex, frozen numeric policy, and the public validator timed out while noop, strtod, marker, and core-info controls passed.

  • Replaced only the decimal-token std::regex predicate with an allocation-free ASCII full-token parser for the identical frozen grammar. Marker handling, strtod, ERANGE, finite/subnormal/negative policy, diagnostics, and all scientific mapping semantics are unchanged. A fixed-seed 100,000-token old-regex/manual-parser differential is part of every platform RECERT.

  • The Windows harness obtains effective LC_CTYPE, LC_COLLATE, and LC_NUMERIC values through a separate fresh-process bare-C-runtime DLL operation. This avoids a Windows R 4.6.1 crash observed in both individual and combined R-level locale queries without pre-warming D1-D7.

  • Corrected RECERT session-option evidence to distinguish requested from effective values, require the portable scipen=-9/0/999 matrix, and report clamped -999 probes as unavailable rather than exact PASS.

  • Added a bounded Windows 10-tip fresh-process cold-start diagnostic with numeric pre-warm, no-length, fixed/free, wrapper/core, and standalone C++ regex timing controls; the diagnostic does not change scientific semantics.

  • Closed Fix005A gene-ID routes by validating existing object names under the same Unicode-preserving whitespace/control/duplicate rules as gene_ids=, while retaining deterministic auto-fill only for truly missing names.

  • Added a byte-key order assertion before restoring gene-ID encodings so the R wrapper cannot mask a reordered C++ result axis.

  • Replaced single-process deep-tree timeouts with process-tree termination and an independent evidence verifier that rejects timeout rows containing late R completion output.

  • Opened the controlled Fix005/RC002 candidate without moving the frozen, abandoned v0.1.0-rc1 tag.

  • Corrected the SplitAligner paper title associated with DOI 10.64898/2026.02.24.707838 while keeping the top-level CFF title specific to SplitAlignerR software.

  • Hardened explicit gene identifiers, Catnip10 validator failure reporting, Oracle character ordering, and release metadata consistency gates.

  • Froze the first V1 release-candidate identity: package 0.1.0, C++ core 0.1.0, general schema 1.0.0, and paired schema 1.0.0.

  • Added release-candidate provenance, dependency, replay, and multi-platform verification metadata without changing the accepted Fix004 scientific logic.

  • Retained v0.1.0-rc1 as a candidate identifier only; independent RECERT and final release approval remain separate gates.

  • Unified paired finalization under SAR-V1-SEM-003: production and unit tests now use one graph-state/numeric-evidence finalizer.

  • Corrected free_pre_promotion_matrix so structural and topological states remain literal NA until the paired graph-state gate is applied.

  • Rejected unknown or padded graph/finalized tokens as input-quality errors.

  • Removed the redundant legacy_gate_failed ledger field; literal NA and residual_NA remain the only finalized-token and summary representations.

SplitAlignerR 0.0.2.9001

  • Added per-gene retained-taxon provenance and exact fixed/free taxon-set pairing gates.
  • Restored the frozen paired-finalize rule from SAR-V1-SEM-002: literal NA is an intentional finalized token, and residual_NA is only its summary name rather than a graph state or recovery-scoped subtype.
  • Added explicit pre-promotion/final-token provenance and enforced that only finite fixed primitive evidence can promote NA_topo; finite fused evidence never substitutes for that primitive gate.
  • Strengthened persisted-result object invariants and aligned Oracle numeric merging with the production core’s all-or-none finite-evidence policy.
  • Replaced the unreachable singleton-side structural fallback with a loud internal invariant failure and added non-vacuous boundary tests.

SplitAlignerR 0.0.2.9000

  • Implemented the C++17 graph-first empirical mapper exposed by align_branches(), with separate primitive-state and numeric-evidence layers.
  • Added deterministic composite-coordinate provenance and recovery ledgers; fused numeric values live on composite coordinates rather than being copied into primitive cells.
  • Added Newick, line-based file, phylo, multiPhylo, and list input adapters, with fixed-mode mismatch diagnostics and strict taxon/ID validation.
  • Added regression coverage reproducing all 272 Catnip10 primitive cells and all 19 frozen fusion events across both deletion regimes.
  • Added result summaries, member-set provenance queries, checked RDS save/reload, a quick-start vignette, and deterministic random-tree property tests for pruning, terminal, root-representation, and wrapper/core invariants.
  • Added a separate paired-bookkeeping API that preserves frozen fixed/free numeric promotion gates and records residual NA without changing semantic single-tree states.
  • Added an opt-in external regression hook for the frozen 302-mammal example, covering 6,010 fixed/free legacy cell classes without embedding local paths or duplicating the publication authority into the package.
  • Added the first C++17 core boundary with strict whole-token, finite-range branch-length validation and structured diagnostics.
  • Added C++ reference-tree parsing and canonical unrooted coordinate tables with root-representation normalization, quoted-label/annotation handling, and retained multifurcations.
  • Added a pure R node-edge implementation that independently recomputes both bundled Catnip10 graph-oracle scenarios without calling the C++ core or using projected splits.
  • Recorded the V1 scientific, numeric, provenance, and paired-bookkeeping contracts under inst/spec/.
  • Clarified that paired residual_NA summarizes finalized literal NA and is not a fifth graph state.

SplitAlignerR 0.0.2

  • Prepared the package as a public seed release for the SplitAligner R reference implementation track.
  • Reframed the README and package metadata around bundled Catnip10 graph-oracle benchmark data, audit-ready accessors, and validation helpers.
  • Added catnip10_summary_counts(), validate_catnip10_oracle(), catnip10_fusion_groups(), and catnip10_matrix().
  • Removed placeholder software DOI metadata and private local paths from public-facing source files.

SplitAlignerR 0.0.1

  • Initial package scaffold (v0.0.1-scaffold).
  • Bundled the deterministic Catnip10 10-tip coordinate-audit benchmark expected oracle outputs (unrooted axis, both the global and local deletion regimes) as the catnip10_oracle data set, with the catnip10_expected() accessor.
  • Added splitalignerR_scaffold() placeholder so the package installs and passes R CMD check.
  • Set up GitHub Actions R-CMD-check continuous integration.
  • The split-based branch-mapping engine is not implemented yet.
